_metadata.description: Label-efficient preference elicitation via informative pairwise comparison.

requirements.title: Pairwise comparison is the primary elicitation surface
requirements.description: Preference is elicited by asking which of two candidates is preferred, with an explicit no-preference option. Pairwise judgement is used because it carries more information per unit of listener effort than absolute rating, which matters acutely when exactly one person produces every label.

validation.notes: Comparisons update the model; ties are recorded rather than coerced

requirements.title: Pairs are chosen for information, not at random
requirements.description: The next pair is selected to maximise expected reduction in model uncertainty, so few judgements produce a usable model. Random pairing is available only as a measurable baseline.

validation.notes: Active selection reduces posterior uncertainty faster than random baseline

requirements.title: Comparison is robust to a single inconsistent rater
requirements.description: The rating scheme tolerates intransitive and mood-dependent judgements without destabilising, and does not let a small number of early comparisons permanently fix an item's standing.

validation.notes: Intransitive cycles and reversals converge without oscillation or lock-in

requirements.title: Component-level comparison
requirements.description: Comparison can be scoped to an isolated element of a track rather than the whole mix, so the listener can express that they like a bassline without endorsing the vocal over it.

validation.notes: Stem-scoped comparisons update attribute weights without endorsing the parent track
